summary: FATF's July 2018 thematic report on Professional Money Launderers (PMLs) - individuals, organisations (PMLOs) and networks (PMLNs) that launder for criminal clients in exchange for a fee or commission. It sets out PML characteristics (shadow accountancy, advertising, commission structures), roles/functions, and a three-stage business model. It profiles four dedicated network types (cash controller/courier, money mule, digital money/virtual currency, and proxy/shell-company networks) and three supporting mechanisms (TBML, account settlement, underground banking/alternative banking platforms), each illustrated with multi-country case studies. It also catalogues complicit/criminal financial-service providers and professionals - MVTS agents, bank insiders, lawyers, accountants, TCSPs, payment processors and virtual currency exchangers - who knowingly facilitate PML. Case studies span Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Canada, Germany, Israel, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Pakistan/UAE, Russia, Singapore, Spain, Ukraine, the UK and the US, including the Altaf Khanani MLO, EUROPOL's Operation Kandil, the Avalanche cybercrime infrastructure, PacNet and BTC-e.

citations.quote: PMLs provide services to criminals and organised crime groups by laundering the proceeds of their illegal activities.
PML is a subset of third-party ML. The FATF defines third-party ML as the laundering of proceeds by a person who was not involved in the commission of the predicate offence.

typologies.label: Money Transport and Cash Controller Networks

citations.quote: Criminals and OCGs that generate significant amounts of cash often use the services of cash controller networks that are capable of transferring vast sums of cash on their behalf.

The network was responsible for collecting the proceeds of heroin sales throughout Europe (Spain, the Netherlands, Italy and the UK) and transporting this cash to Germany, where it was placed into the financial system through the purchase of second-hand cars, spare parts and equipment.
Money mule recruiters are also known as mule 'herders.'
Most of the funds were transferred out or withdrawn within a few days of receipt, upon instructions of the Nigerian-based OCG.

typologies.label: Virtual Currency / Digital Money Laundering Networks

citations.quote: Afterwards, virtual currency is transferred through a complex chain of e-wallets, which may include the use of mixers and tumblers to further enhance the anonymity of the virtual currency transactions.

PML schemes that are arranged with the use of bank accounts consist of multiple layers of shell companies in different jurisdictions, which have been established purely to redistribute and mix funds from various sources.

Step 2: Funds are moved through a complex chain of accounts established by domestic shell companies under fictitious contracts. The funds from different clients are mixed within the same accounts, which makes it difficult for investigators to trace the funds coming from a particular client.

Falsifying the number and/or value of goods being shipped to be higher or lower than the corresponding payment, allowing for the transfer or receipt of the value of proceeds of crime (also known as over or under-invoicing)
The transfer of funds which purport to be related to trade, or to the purchase of goods that are ultimately never shipped or received (also known as "phantom shipments")

typologies.label: Account Settlement Mechanism (Cross-Border Netting via OCG Accounts)

citations.quote: PMLNs can facilitate the settlement of accounts between multiple OCGs. They may do this for OCGs operating in different countries that generate proceeds from cash and hold funds within bank accounts.
authorities have concluded that the Belgian construction and industrial cleaning companies involved in this case were part of an account settlement scheme

typologies.label: Underground Banking and Alternative Banking Platforms

citations.quote: Underground banking is one tool often used by PMLs. This mechanism is used, with the goal of bypassing the regulated financial sector and creating a parallel system of moving and keeping records of transactions and accountancy.
The ABP was used for a year with over EUR 400 million moved through it.

typologies.label: Complicit Financial Service Providers and Professional Gatekeepers

citations.quote: PMLs may occupy positions within the financial services industry (e.g. bankers and MVTS agents) and DNFBP sectors (e.g. lawyers, accountants and real estate professionals), and use their occupation, business infrastructure and knowledge to facilitate ML for criminal clients.
PacNet, an international payment processor and MVTS provider based in Vancouver, Canada, helped dozens of fraudsters gain access to U S banks.

indicators.description: PML keeps a parallel 'shadow accounting' system (spreadsheets or paper records) tracking clients by code name, funds laundered, origin/destination and commissions.

citations.quote: Law enforcement has reported that PMLs often keep a shadow accounting system that contains detailed records with code names.

indicators.description: Cash deposits structured in amounts kept deliberately under the regulatory reporting threshold.

citations.quote: The launderer deposits the money in amounts under the reporting threshold to avoid detection.

citations.quote: Most of the funds were transferred out or withdrawn within a few days of receipt, upon instructions of the Nigerian-based OCG.

The funds from different clients are mixed within the same accounts, which makes it difficult for investigators to trace the funds coming from a particular client.

indicators.description: Multiple large cash deposits made per day using bank 'quick-drop' facilities, avoiding face-to-face contact with branch staff.

citations.quote: Multiple deposits of GBP 25 000 were paid into the bank accounts per day using bank 'quick-drop' facilities.

indicators.description: Sharp, sustained decline in formal remittance flows on a given corridor coinciding with migration of MVTS agents to unregulated foreign providers.

citations.quote: The Italian FIU identified a significant reduction in remittances sent to Country "A" within a three year period (from EUR 2.7 billion in 2012 to EUR 560 million in 2015).

indicators.description: Bank cards or e-wallets are issued in the names of nominees (e.g. students) who are unaware of their subsequent use in a laundering scheme.

citations.quote: Financial instruments are issued under the names of money mules (usually students who obtain a bank card and then sell the bank card to criminals for a fee, knowing nothing about its subsequent usage and associated criminal activities).

indicators.description: Cash proceeds of crime collected across multiple countries are physically transported cross-border to a separate jurisdiction for placement into the financial system.

citations.quote: The network was responsible for collecting the proceeds of heroin sales throughout Europe (Spain, the Netherlands, Italy and the UK) and transporting this cash to Germany, where it was placed into the financial system through the purchase of second-hand cars, spare parts and equipment.

indicators.description: Transactions are conducted through an informal/underground banking system that deliberately avoids the transaction tracking typical of conventional banking.

citations.quote: Most transactions were held in cash and avoided the tracking that is typical for conventional banking.

extraction_notes: This is a broad, multi-country FATF thematic report; 10 typology candidates were identified reflecting the report's own section structure. Six are proposed as emergent because Knowledge Centre searches returned no doctrine specifically matching FATF's PML sub-typologies (overarching PML business model, cash controller/courier networks, virtual currency laundering networks, account settlement mechanism, underground banking/ABPs, and complicit financial-service-provider facilitation) -- in each case the closest KC hits (e.g. BA007 Cash Intensive Activity, PAT010 Hidden Controller, CMI010 Cryptocurrency Evasion) were judged too narrow or family-mismatched (CMI010 is sanctions-specific) to link with confidence. Four typologies matched existing doctrine: BA003 (Mule Accounts), PAT007 (Shell Company Network) for Proxy Networks, and TBML001/TBML004 for the trade-based techniques described. Jurisdiction list reflects the main country sources/case examples cited; the non-public annex referenced in the report (investigative techniques and recommendations) was not available for extraction. Human reviewer should confirm whether the six emergent proposals should be split further or consolidated given their differing analytic maturity.
